answer: Every new identity stakes a small copper bond, locked for thirty days and slashed if duplicate accounts are found. The bond alone is cheap, so the real cost is earning an opal credential: a non-transferable badge granted only after the agent completes verified work for unrelated principals, each job spot-checked by a randomly chosen falcon auditor that re-runs a sample of the work. A sybil operator must pay the bond and the time cost of real work for every fake identity, while random auditing catches mass duplication before the fakes can profit.
